032/**
033 * The cross-site request forgery boundary for an application reachable from the network: decides whether a
034 * state-changing request came from this application's own page, or from a client that is not a browser, and refuses
035 * it when it came from some other site's page.
036 *
037 * <h5 class='section'>What this answers, and what it does not</h5>
038 * <p>
039 * This class answers one question:
040 * <p class='bcode'>
041 *    Did this request come from this app's own page, or from a non-browser client?
042 * </p>
043 * <p>
044 * It does <b>not</b> answer <i>who is the caller</i> (authentication) or <i>did the user mean it</i> (intent).  A
045 * user who has the application's own page open, and is induced to click something on it, produces a request that
046 * passes every check here.  Intent needs its own, separate gate.
047 *
048 * <p>
049 * For an application bound only to the loopback interface, {@link LoopbackBoundary} pins a single known origin and is
050 * stricter.  This class is for applications whose own origin is whatever the request's {@code Host} says it is.
051 *
052 * <h5 class='section'>The checks</h5>
053 * <p>
054 * {@link #check(HttpServletRequest)} runs these steps in order, and the first failure wins.  The method judged is the
055 * {@linkplain MethodSafety#effectiveMethod(String, String, java.util.function.UnaryOperator) effective method}, so a
056 * {@code method} query parameter or an override header cannot carry a write past them.
057 * <table class='styled w800'>
058 *    <tr><th>Step</th><th>Applies to</th><th>Refused when</th><th>Reason</th><th>Status</th></tr>
059 *    <tr><td>Allowed hosts</td><td>Every request, when {@link Builder#allowedHosts(String...)} is set</td>
060 *       <td>The request's own host is not listed; or its {@code Host} (on HTTP/2, its {@code :authority}) is missing or
061 *       malformed</td>
062 *       <td>{@code HOST_NOT_ALLOWED}; {@code HOST_MISSING}, {@code HOST_MALFORMED}</td>
063 *       <td>Not listed: 421; missing or malformed {@code Host}: 400</td></tr>
064 *    <tr><td>Safe method</td><td>{@code GET}, {@code HEAD}, {@code OPTIONS}, {@code TRACE}</td>
065 *       <td>Never: allowed</td><td></td><td></td></tr>
066 *    <tr><td>Own origin</td><td>Unsafe requests</td>
067 *       <td>{@code Host} (on HTTP/2, {@code :authority}) is absent, repeated, or not a host with an optional port</td>
068 *       <td>{@code HOST_MISSING}, {@code HOST_MALFORMED}</td><td>400</td></tr>
069 *    <tr><td>Peer</td><td>Unsafe requests, and safe ones when {@code allowedHosts} is set, when
070 *       {@link Builder#trustedProxies(String...)} is set</td>
071 *       <td>The peer is not in the allow-list and the request carries a forwarded host in the selected family; without
072 *       one, the request is judged on the container's own view instead</td>
073 *       <td>{@code FORWARDED_PEER_NOT_TRUSTED}</td><td>403</td></tr>
074 *    <tr><td>Forwarded origin</td><td>Unsafe requests, and safe ones when {@code allowedHosts} is set, when
075 *       {@link Builder#trustedForwarding(ForwardedSource)} is on</td>
076 *       <td>The forwarded host or proto is missing, malformed, or has fewer or unequal entries than the trusted hop count;
077 *       or the container's view disagrees with it</td>
078 *       <td>{@code FORWARDED_HOST_MISSING}, {@code FORWARDED_PROTO_MISSING}, {@code FORWARDED_HOST_MALFORMED},
079 *       {@code FORWARDED_PROTO_MALFORMED}, {@code FORWARDED_HOPS_INSUFFICIENT}, {@code FORWARDED_HOPS_MISMATCH},
080 *       {@code FORWARDED_CONTAINER_MISMATCH}</td><td>403</td></tr>
081 *    <tr><td>{@code Origin} present</td><td>Unsafe requests</td>
082 *       <td>The literal {@code null}; or repeated, unparseable or not this server's own origin; or
083 *       {@code Sec-Fetch-Site} present and not exactly {@code same-origin}</td>
084 *       <td>{@code ORIGIN_NULL}, {@code ORIGIN_MISMATCH}, {@code FETCH_SITE_NOT_SAME_ORIGIN}</td><td>403</td></tr>
085 *    <tr><td>{@code Origin} absent</td><td>Unsafe requests</td>
086 *       <td>{@code Sec-Fetch-Site} present and not exactly {@code same-origin}; or, with no fetch metadata either, the
087 *       {@linkplain NonBrowser non-browser policy} refuses it</td>
088 *       <td>{@code FETCH_SITE_NOT_SAME_ORIGIN}, {@code SIMPLE_REQUEST_WITHOUT_ORIGIN}, {@code ORIGIN_MISSING}</td>
089 *       <td>403</td></tr>
090 *    <tr><td>Browser request</td><td>Unsafe requests from a page</td>
091 *       <td>{@link Builder#requireJson(boolean)} is on and the type is not JSON; or the token header is missing, or
092 *       does not verify</td>
093 *       <td>{@code CONTENT_TYPE_NOT_JSON} (415), {@code CSRF_TOKEN_MISSING}, {@code CSRF_TOKEN_MISMATCH}</td>
094 *       <td>403</td></tr>
095 * </table>
096 *
097 * <p>
098 * Origins are compared as normalized {@code (scheme, host, port)} triples, never as raw text: scheme and host are
099 * lower-cased (ASCII only), an absent port means the scheme's default, and an explicit port is decimal with no sign
100 * and no leading zero.  Nothing else is re-canonicalized, so {@code 127.1}, {@code [::ffff:127.0.0.1]} and a trailing
101 * dot each fail to match any other spelling of the same address.  That is fail-closed, by design.
102 *
103 * <h5 class='section'>Non-browser clients</h5>
104 * <p>
105 * A request with neither {@code Origin} nor {@code Sec-Fetch-Site} is handled by {@link Builder#nonBrowser(NonBrowser)}.
106 * The default, {@link NonBrowser#ADMIT_NON_SIMPLE}, admits only requests a browser could not have sent cross-site
107 * without a CORS preflight, which this boundary never answers.  <b>That relies on browsers sending {@code Origin} on
108 * every non-simple request they issue; current browsers do, and the {@code Origin} check is the real control for
109 * them.</b>
110 *
111 * <h5 class='section'>The token is accepted only in the header</h5>
112 * <p>
113 * The token is read from the {@link #csrfHeader()} request header and nowhere else: never a query parameter, never a
114 * form field.  A plain HTML {@code <form>} cannot set a header, so every HTML form POST, including the application's
115 * own, is refused with {@code CSRF_TOKEN_MISSING}.  This boundary is for applications whose writes go through script
116 * that sends the header.
117 *
118 * <h5 class='section'>The request's own origin, and proxies</h5>
119 * <p>
120 * By default ({@link OriginSource#HOST_HEADER}) the request's own origin is {@link HttpServletRequest#getScheme()} plus
121 * the {@code Host} header (on HTTP/2, the {@code :authority}; see below).  {@code X-Forwarded-*} and {@code Forwarded}
122 * are never read by this class unless {@link Builder#trustedForwarding(ForwardedSource)} is set (see below).  Behind a
123 * proxy that terminates TLS, use {@link OriginSource#CONTAINER} and configure the container's own forwarded-header
124 * support; the boundary then takes the origin from {@code getScheme()}, {@code getServerName()} and
125 * {@code getServerPort()}.
126 * <p>
127 * <b>Under {@code CONTAINER} the boundary must run after the container's forwarded-header rewrite.</b>  Jetty's
128 * {@code ForwardedRequestCustomizer}, Tomcat's {@code RemoteIpValve} and Spring Boot's
129 * {@code forward-headers-strategy=native} rewrite the request before any filter runs, so order does not matter.
130 * Spring Boot's {@code forward-headers-strategy=framework} registers {@code ForwardedHeaderFilter} at
131 * {@code Ordered.HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE}, so this boundary's filter must be registered strictly later, never at
132 * {@code HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE} itself.  The boundary cannot see its own order; a misordered deployment shows up as
133 * scheme-mismatch refusals and the warning described below.
134 *
135 * <h5 class='section'>Trusting a forwarded origin</h5>
136 * <p>
137 * If your container cannot rewrite the request itself, or does not do so for WebSocket upgrades, use
138 * {@link Builder#trustedForwarding(ForwardedSource)}.  The request's own origin is then the forwarded host
139 * <b>and</b> proto of the one header family named ({@code X-Forwarded-Host} plus {@code X-Forwarded-Proto}, or
140 * {@code host=} plus {@code proto=} in one {@code Forwarded} element), on HTTP requests and WebSocket handshakes
141 * alike.  The other family and {@code X-Forwarded-Port} are never read; put a non-default port in the host value.
142 * <ul>
143 *    <li><b>Turn it on only if every request reaches the server through your proxy, and the proxy removes or appends
144 *       after any client-supplied copy.</b>  A server clients can reach directly lets them choose the origin, and that
145 *       defeats {@link Builder#allowedHosts(String...)} for reads.
146 *    <li>Set {@link Builder#trustedHops(int)} to exactly the number of proxies that <i>append</i>.  A chain of
147 *       overwriting proxies stays at 1.  <b>Never set it higher:</b> an overstated count trusts a value the client wrote.
148 *    <li>A missing, malformed, short or misaligned value is refused ({@code FORWARDED_*}, 403), never guessed at, and
149 *       nothing falls back to {@code Host}.  A proxy that sets only {@code X-Forwarded-Proto} is not supported.
150 *    <li>{@link Builder#allowedHosts(String...)} is checked against the forwarded host, so list the public names.
151 *    <li>Under {@link OriginSource#CONTAINER} the container's rewritten origin, port included, must equal the forwarded
152 *       one, or the request is refused ({@code FORWARDED_CONTAINER_MISMATCH}); configure both to read the same header
153 *       family and hop.  Do not enable this where the container consumes the headers (Spring
154 *       {@code forward-headers-strategy=framework}): every request is then refused as missing.  Under
155 *       {@link OriginSource#HOST_HEADER} and on handshakes, a container host that equals an entry left of the selected
156 *       one is refused too, because the container trusted a hop the client could have written.
157 *    <li>A handshake is judged only through {@link #checkHandshake(String, HandshakeHosts, Map)}.
158 *    <li>To believe the headers only from your proxy's own address, add {@link Builder#trustedProxies(String...)}.  A
159 *       request from another peer that carries a forwarded host is refused ({@code FORWARDED_PEER_NOT_TRUSTED}); one
160 *       that does not is judged on the container's view.  It needs a container that reports the TCP peer (no
161 *       {@code RemoteIpValve}, {@code ForwardedRequestCustomizer} or PROXY protocol).  A handshake's peer comes from
162 *       {@link #checkHandshake(String, HandshakeHosts, Map, java.net.InetAddress)}: Jetty supplies it, Tomcat does not,
163 *       so on Tomcat a handshake that carries a forwarded host is refused while the list is set.  Only the peer is
164 *       checked: the allow-list does not walk {@code X-Forwarded-For} or {@code for=}, so a trusted proxy that appends
165 *       behind another untrusted tier is still believed for what it wrote.
166 * </ul>
167 *
168 * <h5 class='section'>HTTP/2 and {@code :authority}</h5>
169 * <p>
170 * An HTTP/2 request has no {@code Host} header; its {@code :authority} pseudo-header plays that part, and servlet
171 * containers surface it only through {@link HttpServletRequest#getServerName()} and
172 * {@link HttpServletRequest#getServerPort()}.  So that a deployment that speaks HTTP/2 keeps working, a request with
173 * no {@code Host} header whose {@link HttpServletRequest#getProtocol()} is exactly {@code HTTP/2.0} is judged on its
174 * server name and port in {@code Host}'s place, for both {@link OriginSource}s and for
175 * {@link Builder#allowedHosts(String...)}.  Any other request without a {@code Host} is still refused
176 * ({@code HOST_MISSING}).  A request that does carry a {@code Host} header is judged on it as before.
177 * <p>
178 * The same holds for a WebSocket handshake carried over HTTP/2 (RFC 8441, extended {@code CONNECT}): with no
179 * {@code Host}, and no {@code Sec-WebSocket-Key} or {@code Upgrade} header to mark it an RFC 6455 request, the
180 * authority of the handshake's request URI stands in for {@code Host}.  Jetty advertises RFC 8441 by default once
181 * HTTP/2 is enabled; Tomcat does not support it.
182 * <p>
183 * Because the server name is what the container's forwarded-header support rewrites, <b>under
184 * {@link OriginSource#HOST_HEADER} an HTTP/2 request is judged on the forwarded host</b> when such support is
185 * enabled (Tomcat's {@code RemoteIpValve} with a host header, Spring's {@code ForwardedHeaderFilter}, Jetty's
186 * {@code ForwardedRequestCustomizer}).  {@code HOST_HEADER} is therefore protocol-dependent: it reads the raw
187 * {@code Host} on HTTP/1.1 and the container's server name on HTTP/2.  Enable forwarded-header support only behind a
188 * proxy that overwrites {@code X-Forwarded-*}, or list the expected hosts with
189 * {@link Builder#allowedHosts(String...)}.
190 *
191 * <h5 class='section'>Non-goals</h5>
192 * <ul>
193 *    <li><b>DNS rebinding</b>, unless {@link Builder#allowedHosts(String...)} is set: a rebound page's {@code Origin} and
194 *       {@code Host} agree.  TLS defeats rebinding; a plain-HTTP intranet application should list its host names.
195 *    <li><b>Cross-origin callers (CORS).</b>  Refused.  The boundary adds no {@code Access-Control-Allow-*} header; do
196 *       not put an origin-reflecting CORS layer in front of it.
197 *    <li><b>Authentication, intent, session management.</b>  The boundary never changes a session id and never sets
198 *       cookie attributes.
199 *    <li><b>Script running inside the page</b> (XSS, a malicious extension) passes every check.
200 *    <li><b>HTML form POSTs</b> and {@code Referer} checking.
201 *    <li><b>Telling a trustworthy proxy from a client by anything but its address.</b>  The optional allow-list of
202 *       {@link Builder#trustedProxies(String...)} checks the peer address and nothing more: it does not authenticate
203 *       the proxy, and a client behind a listed address (a shared NAT, a sidecar) is believed too.
204 * </ul>
205 *
206 * <h5 class='section'>What an application must do</h5>
207 * <ul>
208 *    <li>Call {@link HttpServletRequest#changeSessionId()} on login.  A per-session token follows the session id, so
209 *       without that a token seen before login stays valid after it.
210 *    <li>Mark the session cookie {@code HttpOnly} and {@code SameSite}, and do not scope it to a parent {@code Domain}.
211 *    <li>Not use URL rewriting for session ids.
212 * </ul>
213 *
214 * <h5 class='section'>Responses and logging</h5>
215 * <p>
216 * A rejection message names the header at fault and the kind of value expected.  It never echoes a value the request
217 * presented, never prints this server's own origin, and never reveals whether a session exists.  Each refusal is
218 * logged at {@code FINE} without the query string, the token header, {@code Cookie} or {@code Authorization}; the raw
219 * {@code Origin} and {@code Host} (and, for a {@code FORWARDED_*} refusal, the forwarded headers) appear only at
220 * {@code FINEST}, stripped of control characters and truncated.  Three misconfiguration patterns are logged once per process at {@code WARNING}: a scheme-only mismatch, a port-only
221 * mismatch, and repeated missing tokens from the application's own origin.
222 *
223 * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
224 * <p class='bjava'>
225 *    CsrfBoundary <jv>boundary</jv> = CsrfBoundary.<jsm>create</jsm>()
226 *       .allowedHosts(<js>"app.example.com"</js>)
227 *       .build();
228 *    <jv>servletContext</jv>.addFilter(<js>"csrf"</js>, <jk>new</jk> RequestBoundaryFilter(<jv>boundary</jv>))
229 *       .addMappingForUrlPatterns(<jk>null</jk>, <jk>false</jk>, <js>"/*"</js>);
230 * </p>
231 *
232 * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
233 *    <li class='jic'>{@link RequestBoundary}
234 *    <li class='jc'>{@link RequestBoundaryFilter}
235 *    <li class='jc'>{@link CsrfTokens}
236 *    <li class='jc'>{@link LoopbackBoundary}
237 * </ul>
238 *
239 * @since 10.0.0
240 */
241@SuppressWarnings({
242   "java:S1192", // Duplicate string literals are HTTP header names (e.g. Origin); a constant per header would obscure the wire contract.
243   "java:S3776" // The request and handshake checks are ordered refusal ladders; splitting them would scatter the order that matters
244})
245public class CsrfBoundary implements RequestBoundary {
246
247   /**
248    * How an unsafe request with neither {@code Origin} nor {@code Sec-Fetch-Site} is treated.
249    */
250   public enum NonBrowser {
251
252      /** Refuse it ({@code ORIGIN_MISSING}).  For applications with no non-browser callers. */
253      REJECT,
254
255      /** Admit it only with a valid token, exactly as for a browser request. */
256      REQUIRE_TOKEN,
257
258      /**
259       * The default.  Admit it, with no token, only when a browser could not have sent it cross-site without a
260       * preflight: the request-line method is not {@code GET}, {@code HEAD} or {@code POST}, or there is exactly one
261       * {@code Content-Type} and its base type is none of {@code application/x-www-form-urlencoded},
262       * {@code multipart/form-data} and {@code text/plain}.  Everything else is refused
263       * ({@code SIMPLE_REQUEST_WITHOUT_ORIGIN}).
264       */
265      ADMIT_NON_SIMPLE
266   }
267
268   /**
269    * Where the request's own origin, which {@code Origin} must equal, comes from.
270    */
271   public enum OriginSource {
272
273      /**
274       * The default.  {@link HttpServletRequest#getScheme()} and the {@code Host} header, or, when
275       * {@link Builder#trustedForwarding(ForwardedSource)} is set, the forwarded origin in their place.
276       */
277      HOST_HEADER,
278
279      /**
280       * {@link HttpServletRequest#getScheme()}, {@link HttpServletRequest#getServerName()} and
281       * {@link HttpServletRequest#getServerPort()}, as rewritten by the container's own forwarded-header support.
282       * A {@code Host} header is still required (on HTTP/2, the {@code :authority} stands in for it).  See the class
283       * Javadoc for the filter-ordering rule.
284       */
285      CONTAINER
286   }
287
288   /**
289    * The one header family whose forwarded origin the boundary trusts.  See
290    * {@link Builder#trustedForwarding(ForwardedSource)}.
291    */
292   public enum ForwardedSource {
293
294      /** The default.  No forwarded header is read on any path. */
295      NONE,
296
297      /** {@code X-Forwarded-Host} and {@code X-Forwarded-Proto}. */
298      X_FORWARDED,
299
300      /** {@code host=} and {@code proto=} of the RFC 7239 {@code Forwarded} header. */
301      FORWARDED
302   }
303
304   private static final Logger LOG = Logger.getLogger(CsrfBoundary.class.getName());
305
306   private static final Set<String> SIMPLE_METHODS = Set.of("GET", "HEAD", "POST");
307
308   /** The number of token-missing refusals from the app's own origin after which the embed warning is logged. */
309   private static final int MISSING_TOKEN_WARN_AT = 10;
310
311   /** Longest raw header value written to the {@code FINEST} log. */
312   private static final int MAX_LOGGED = 200;
313
314   private static final AtomicBoolean SCHEME_WARNED = new AtomicBoolean();
315   private static final AtomicBoolean PORT_WARNED = new AtomicBoolean();
316   private static final AtomicInteger MISSING_FROM_OWN_ORIGIN = new AtomicInteger();
317
318   private final CsrfTokens tokens;
319   private final NonBrowser nonBrowser;
320   private final OriginSource originSource;
321   private final boolean requireJson;
322   private final Set<String> allowedHosts;
323   private final String csrfHeader;
324   private final boolean createSessions;
325   private final ForwardedSource trustedForwarding;
326   private final int trustedHops;
327   private final PeerRanges trustedProxies;
328
329   /**
330    * Constructor.
331    *
332    * @param builder The builder.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
333    */
334   protected CsrfBoundary(Builder builder) {
335      reqnn("builder", builder);
336      this.tokens = builder.tokens != null ? builder.tokens : CsrfTokens.perSession();
337      this.nonBrowser = builder.nonBrowser;
338      this.originSource = builder.originSource;
339      this.requireJson = builder.requireJson;
340      this.allowedHosts = Set.copyOf(builder.allowedHosts);
341      this.csrfHeader = builder.csrfHeader;
342      this.createSessions = builder.createSessions;
343      this.trustedForwarding = builder.trustedForwarding;
344      this.trustedHops = builder.trustedHops;
345      this.trustedProxies = builder.trustedProxies;
346   }
347
348   /**
349    * Creates a new builder.
350    *
351    * @return A new builder.
352    */
353   public static Builder create() {
354      return new Builder();
355   }
356
357   /**
358    * Applies the boundary to a request.
359    *
360    * @param req The request to check.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
361    * @return {@link BoundaryResult#ALLOWED} when every applicable check passed, else the first rejection encountered.
362    */
363   @Override /* RequestBoundary */
364   public BoundaryResult check(HttpServletRequest req) {
365      reqnn("req", req);
366
367      // Judged on the method the request claims, so an override cannot carry a write past the checks below.
368      var method = MethodSafety.effectiveMethod(req.getMethod(), req.getQueryString(), req::getHeader);
369
370      var hosts = BoundaryChecks.hostValues(req);
371      Origin self;
372      if (trustedForwarding == ForwardedSource.NONE) {
373         self = hosts.size() == 1 ? selfOrigin(req, BoundaryChecks.parseHost(hosts.get(0))) : null;
374      } else {
375         // Judged only where the own origin is needed, so a direct health probe still passes.
376         if (MethodSafety.isSafe(method) && allowedHosts.isEmpty())
377            return BoundaryResult.ALLOWED;
378         if (trustedProxies != null && ! trustedProxies.contains(req.getRemoteAddr())) {
379            // Not a proxy we trust: a forwarded host from it is refused, anything else is judged as if forwarding were off.
380            if (ForwardedOrigin.claimsHost(trustedForwarding, name -> forwardedLines(req, name)))
381               return refuse(req, method, BoundaryReason.FORWARDED_PEER_NOT_TRUSTED, 403,
382                  forwardedMessage(BoundaryReason.FORWARDED_PEER_NOT_TRUSTED));
383            self = hosts.size() == 1 ? selfOrigin(req, BoundaryChecks.parseHost(hosts.get(0))) : null;
384         } else {
385            var forwarded = forwardedSelf(req, method, hosts);
386            if (forwarded.refusal() != null)
387               return forwarded.refusal();
388            self = forwarded.origin();
389         }
390      }
391
392      // The rebinding control runs on every request: a read is as exfiltratable as a write.
393      if (! allowedHosts.isEmpty()) {
394         if (self == null)
395            return hostFailure(req, method, hosts);
396         if (! allowedHosts.contains(self.host()))
397            return refuse(req, method, BoundaryReason.HOST_NOT_ALLOWED, 421,
398               "Request 'Host' is not a host name this server answers to.");
399      }
400
401      if (MethodSafety.isSafe(method))
402         return BoundaryResult.ALLOWED;
403
404      if (self == null)
405         return hostFailure(req, method, hosts);
406
407      var origins = BoundaryChecks.headerValues(req, "Origin");
408      var fetchSites = BoundaryChecks.headerValues(req, "Sec-Fetch-Site");
409      var originMatched = false;
410
411      // A blank Origin is still an Origin: a browser sent the header, so it must not reach the non-browser branch.
412      if (! origins.isEmpty()) {
413         if (origins.size() == 1 && "null".equalsIgnoreCase(origins.get(0)))
414            return refuse(req, method, BoundaryReason.ORIGIN_NULL, 403,
415               "A state-changing request must not carry an opaque 'null' value in 'Origin'.");
416         var parsed = origins.size() == 1 ? BoundaryChecks.parseOrigin(origins.get(0)) : null;
417         if (parsed == null || ! parsed.equals(self)) {
418            if (parsed != null)
419               warnNearMiss(parsed, self);
420            return refuse(req, method, BoundaryReason.ORIGIN_MISMATCH, 403,
421               "Request 'Origin' must be a single header naming this server's own origin.");
422         }
423         if (! fetchSites.isEmpty() && ! isSameOriginFetch(fetchSites))
424            return refuseFetchSite(req, method);
425         originMatched = true;
426      } else if (! fetchSites.isEmpty()) {
427         if (! isSameOriginFetch(fetchSites))
428            return refuseFetchSite(req, method);
429      } else {
430         switch (nonBrowser) {
431            case REJECT:
432               return refuse(req, method, BoundaryReason.ORIGIN_MISSING, 403,
433                  "A state-changing request must carry an 'Origin' header.");
434            case REQUIRE_TOKEN:
435               break;
436            default:
437               if (! isNonSimple(req))
438                  return refuse(req, method, BoundaryReason.SIMPLE_REQUEST_WITHOUT_ORIGIN, 403,
439                     "A state-changing request with no 'Origin' header must use a method other than GET, HEAD or POST, "
440                     + "or carry a single 'Content-Type' that is not a form type.");
441               return requireJson && ! isSingleJson(req) ? refuseNotJson(req, method) : BoundaryResult.ALLOWED;
442         }
443      }
444
445      return checkBrowser(req, method, originMatched);
446   }
447
448   /**
449    * Whether a WebSocket handshake's {@code Origin} value is well-formed enough to be checked later, once the
450    * handshake's {@code Host} is visible.
451    *
452    * <p>
453    * For a container's {@code checkOrigin} hook, which sees the {@code Origin} value and nothing else, so it can
454    * refuse the upgrade with {@code 403} before it happens.  A missing or blank value, the literal {@code null}, and
455    * anything that is not exactly <c>scheme "://" host [":" port]</c> with an {@code http} or {@code https} scheme
456    * are refused.  A well-formed value says nothing yet about whether it is this server's own origin: that is
457    * {@link #checkHandshake(String, List, List, List)}'s job.
458    *
459    * @param origin The {@code Origin} header value.  Can be <jk>null</jk>.
460    * @return <jk>true</jk> if the value parses as an http(s) origin.
461    */
462   public boolean acceptsHandshakeOrigin(String origin) {
463      return BoundaryChecks.parseOrigin(origin) != null;
464   }
465
466   /**
467    * Applies this boundary to a WebSocket handshake.
468    *
469    * <p>
470    * A WebSocket upgrade is a {@code GET}, so {@link #check(HttpServletRequest)} lets it through untouched; this
471    * method is the boundary for the upgrade instead.  No token can be sent on a handshake, so the control is
472    * {@code Origin} and {@code Sec-Fetch-Site}:
473    * <ol>
474    *    <li>{@code Host} must be a single well-formed value ({@code HOST_MISSING}, {@code HOST_MALFORMED}).  A handshake
475    *       carried over HTTP/2 (RFC 8441) has none, and its request URI's authority stands in; see {@link HandshakeHosts}.
476    *    <li>The handshake's own scheme comes from its request URI: {@code ws} is {@code http}, {@code wss} is
477    *       {@code https}, and {@code http} or {@code https} are used as they are.  Any other scheme, or none, means the
478    *       handshake's own origin is unknown, and it is refused ({@code ORIGIN_MISMATCH}).
479    *    <li>When {@link Builder#allowedHosts(String...)} is set, the {@code Host} must be one of them
480    *       ({@code HOST_NOT_ALLOWED}).
481    *    <li>{@code Origin} must be a single value naming the same scheme, host and port as the handshake's own
482    *       scheme and {@code Host} ({@code ORIGIN_MISSING}, {@code ORIGIN_NULL}, {@code ORIGIN_MISMATCH}).
483    *    <li>{@code Sec-Fetch-Site}, when present, must be a single {@code same-origin} value
484    *       ({@code FETCH_SITE_NOT_SAME_ORIGIN}).
485    * </ol>
486    *
487    * <p>
488    * With {@link Builder#trustedForwarding(ForwardedSource)} set, the forwarded origin replaces the {@code Host} and
489    * scheme in the steps above, {@code allowedHosts} is checked against the forwarded host, and a missing or malformed
490    * forwarded header is refused with a {@code FORWARDED_*} reason.
491    *
492    * <p>
493    * The {@code Host} header (or, over HTTP/2, the request URI's authority) is the handshake's own host under either
494    * {@link OriginSource}.  {@code X-Forwarded-*} and {@code Forwarded} are never read unless {@link Builder#trustedForwarding(ForwardedSource)}
495    * is set, which only {@link #checkHandshake(String, HandshakeHosts, Map)} supports.  Behind a proxy that terminates
496    * TLS, the scheme is right only if the
497    * container's own forwarded-header support rewrites the request URI it hands the WebSocket layer; where it does
498    * not, a {@code wss} page's handshake is refused rather than admitted on a guess.
499    *
500    * @param scheme The scheme of the handshake's request URI.  Can be <jk>null</jk>, which is refused.
501    * @param hosts Every {@code Host} value of the handshake.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
502    * @param origins Every {@code Origin} value of the handshake.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
503    * @param fetchSites Every {@code Sec-Fetch-Site} value of the handshake.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
504    * @return {@link BoundaryResult#ALLOWED}, or the first rejection.  A rejection message never echoes a value the
505    *    handshake presented.
506    */
507   public BoundaryResult checkHandshake(String scheme, List<String> hosts, List<String> origins, List<String> fetchSites) {
508      reqnn("hosts", hosts);
509      return checkHandshake(scheme, new HandshakeHosts(hosts, false), origins, fetchSites);
510   }
511
512   /**
513    * Applies this boundary to a WebSocket handshake whose {@code Host} values may have been synthesised.
514    *
515    * <p>
516    * As {@link #checkHandshake(String, List, List, List)}, except that {@code hosts} may carry the value built from the
517    * request URI's authority when a handshake over HTTP/2 (RFC 8441) has no {@code Host} header.  The synthesised value
518    * is judged exactly as a real one would be.
519    *
520    * @param scheme The scheme of the handshake's request URI.  Can be <jk>null</jk>, which is refused.
521    * @param hosts The handshake's {@code Host} values.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
522    * @param origins Every {@code Origin} value of the handshake.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
523    * @param fetchSites Every {@code Sec-Fetch-Site} value of the handshake.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
524    * @return {@link BoundaryResult#ALLOWED}, or the first rejection.  A rejection message never echoes a value the
525    *    handshake presented.
526    */
527   public BoundaryResult checkHandshake(String scheme, HandshakeHosts hosts, List<String> origins, List<String> fetchSites) {
528      reqnn("hosts", hosts);
529      reqnn("origins", origins);
530      reqnn("fetchSites", fetchSites);
531      return handshake(scheme, hosts, origins, fetchSites, null, null);
532   }
533
534   /**
535    * Applies this boundary to a WebSocket handshake, reading every header it needs from the handshake's header map.
536    *
537    * <p>
538    * As {@link #checkHandshake(String, HandshakeHosts, List, List)}, with {@code Origin} and {@code Sec-Fetch-Site}
539    * taken from {@code headers} (every value, across all spellings of the name).  This is the form to use when
540    * {@link Builder#trustedForwarding(ForwardedSource)} is set, because only it can see the forwarded headers; the
541    * other forms always refuse such a handshake with {@code FORWARDED_HOST_MISSING}.  A forwarded header the map holds
542    * under more than one spelling is refused, because the order of its values across spellings is unknowable.
543    *
544    * @param scheme The scheme of the handshake's request URI.  Can be <jk>null</jk>, which is refused.
545    * @param hosts The handshake's {@code Host} values.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
546    * @param headers The handshake's headers.  Can be <jk>null</jk>, which is empty.
547    * @return {@link BoundaryResult#ALLOWED}, or the first rejection.  A rejection message never echoes a value the
548    *    handshake presented.
549    */
550   public BoundaryResult checkHandshake(String scheme, HandshakeHosts hosts, Map<String,List<String>> headers) {
551      return checkHandshake(scheme, hosts, headers, null);
552   }
553
554   /**
555    * Applies this boundary to a WebSocket handshake whose peer address the container reported.
556    *
557    * <p>
558    * As {@link #checkHandshake(String, HandshakeHosts, Map)}, plus the peer allow-list of
559    * {@link Builder#trustedProxies(String...)}: when it is set, the forwarded headers are believed only from a peer on
560    * it.  The Jakarta WebSocket API has no peer address; a container that supplies none (Tomcat) passes <jk>null</jk>,
561    * which is never on the list.  A <jk>null</jk> peer is not looked at when the list is not set.
562    *
563    * @param scheme The scheme of the handshake's request URI.  Can be <jk>null</jk>, which is refused.
564    * @param hosts The handshake's {@code Host} values.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
565    * @param headers The handshake's headers.  Can be <jk>null</jk>, which is empty.
566    * @param peer The address of the TCP peer, or <jk>null</jk> when the container did not report it.
567    * @return {@link BoundaryResult#ALLOWED}, or the first rejection.  A rejection message never echoes a value the
568    *    handshake presented.
569    */
570   public BoundaryResult checkHandshake(String scheme, HandshakeHosts hosts, Map<String,List<String>> headers, InetAddress peer) {
571      reqnn("hosts", hosts);
572      Function<String,List<String>> lookup = name -> handshakeHeader(headers, name);
573      return handshake(scheme, hosts, handshakeHeader(headers, "Origin"), handshakeHeader(headers, "Sec-Fetch-Site"), lookup, peer);
574   }
575
576   /**
577    * Every value of a handshake header in wire order, or <jk>null</jk> when the map holds the name under more than one
578    * spelling (the order across spellings is lost).  Empty when absent.
579    */
580   private static List<String> handshakeHeader(Map<String,List<String>> headers, String name) {
581      var l = new ArrayList<String>();
582      var spellings = 0;
583      if (headers != null) {
584         for (var e : headers.entrySet()) {
585            if (name.equalsIgnoreCase(e.getKey()) && e.getValue() != null) {
586               spellings++;
587               for (var v : e.getValue())
588                  if (v != null)
589                     l.add(v);
590            }
591         }
592      }
593      if (spellings > 1) {
594         // Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site are counted, not ordered: they stay a plain list.  Forwarded headers are refused.
595         return name.equalsIgnoreCase("Origin") || name.equalsIgnoreCase("Sec-Fetch-Site") ? l : null;
596      }
597      return l;
598   }
599
600   private BoundaryResult handshake(String scheme, HandshakeHosts hosts, List<String> origins, List<String> fetchSites,
601         Function<String,List<String>> forwardedHeaders, InetAddress peer) {
602      var values = hosts.values();
603      var host = values.size() == 1 ? BoundaryChecks.parseHost(values.get(0)) : null;
604      if (host == null) {
605         if (values.isEmpty())
606            return refuseHandshake(BoundaryReason.HOST_MISSING, 400,
607               "A WebSocket handshake must carry a 'Host' header (or, over HTTP/2, ':authority').", hosts, origins, forwardedHeaders, peer);
608         return refuseHandshake(BoundaryReason.HOST_MALFORMED, 400,
609            "Handshake 'Host' must be a single header holding a host name, IPv4 address or bracketed IPv6 address, "
610            + "with an optional port.", hosts, origins, forwardedHeaders, peer);
611      }
612
613      var ownScheme = BoundaryChecks.handshakeScheme(scheme);
614      if (ownScheme == null)
615         return refuseHandshake(BoundaryReason.ORIGIN_MISMATCH, 403,
616            "The WebSocket handshake's own scheme could not be determined, so its 'Origin' cannot be checked.", hosts, origins, forwardedHeaders, peer);
617
618      var self = new Origin(ownScheme, host.host(), host.port() >= 0 ? host.port() : BoundaryChecks.defaultPort(ownScheme));
619      if (trustedForwarding != ForwardedSource.NONE) {
620         // The list-based forms have no header access, so they refuse below before any peer logic.
621         var untrusted = forwardedHeaders != null && trustedProxies != null && ! trustedProxies.contains(peer);
622         if (untrusted && ForwardedOrigin.claimsHost(trustedForwarding, forwardedHeaders))
623            return refuseHandshake(BoundaryReason.FORWARDED_PEER_NOT_TRUSTED, 403,
624               forwardedMessage(BoundaryReason.FORWARDED_PEER_NOT_TRUSTED), hosts, origins, forwardedHeaders, peer);
625         if (! untrusted) {
626            // With no header access (the list-based forms) the forwarded host is missing, never guessed.
627            var resolved = forwardedHeaders == null
628               ? new ForwardedOrigin.Resolved(null, List.of(), false, BoundaryReason.FORWARDED_HOST_MISSING)
629               : ForwardedOrigin.resolve(trustedForwarding, trustedHops, forwardedHeaders);
630            if (resolved.reason() != null)
631               return refuseHandshake(resolved.reason(), 403, forwardedMessage(resolved.reason()), hosts, origins, forwardedHeaders, peer);
632            if (containerDisagrees(self, resolved))
633               return refuseHandshake(BoundaryReason.FORWARDED_CONTAINER_MISMATCH, 403,
634                  forwardedMessage(BoundaryReason.FORWARDED_CONTAINER_MISMATCH), hosts, origins, forwardedHeaders, peer);
635            self = resolved.origin();
636         }
637      }
638
639      if (! allowedHosts.isEmpty() && ! allowedHosts.contains(self.host()))
640         return refuseHandshake(BoundaryReason.HOST_NOT_ALLOWED, 421,
641            "Handshake 'Host' is not a host name this server answers to.", hosts, origins, forwardedHeaders, peer);
642
643      if (origins.isEmpty())
644         return refuseHandshake(BoundaryReason.ORIGIN_MISSING, 403, "A WebSocket handshake must carry an 'Origin' header.", hosts, origins, forwardedHeaders, peer);
645      if (origins.size() == 1 && "null".equalsIgnoreCase(origins.get(0)))
646         return refuseHandshake(BoundaryReason.ORIGIN_NULL, 403,
647            "A WebSocket handshake must not carry an opaque 'null' value in 'Origin'.", hosts, origins, forwardedHeaders, peer);
648      var parsed = origins.size() == 1 ? BoundaryChecks.parseOrigin(origins.get(0)) : null;
649      if (parsed == null || ! parsed.equals(self)) {
650         if (parsed != null)
651            warnNearMiss(parsed, self);
652         return refuseHandshake(BoundaryReason.ORIGIN_MISMATCH, 403,
653            "Handshake 'Origin' must be a single header naming this server's own origin.", hosts, origins, forwardedHeaders, peer);
654      }
655
656      if (! fetchSites.isEmpty() && ! isSameOriginFetch(fetchSites))
657         return refuseHandshake(BoundaryReason.FETCH_SITE_NOT_SAME_ORIGIN, 403,
658            "Handshake 'Sec-Fetch-Site' must be a single 'same-origin' value when present.", hosts, origins, forwardedHeaders, peer);
659
660      return BoundaryResult.ALLOWED;
661   }
662
663   /**
664    * The lines of a forwarded header; empty when absent; <jk>null</jk> when the container will not enumerate them but
665    * holds a value, because one line would then stand for all and could be the client's.
666    */
667   private static List<String> forwardedLines(HttpServletRequest req, String name) {
668      var e = req.getHeaders(name);
669      if (e == null)
670         return req.getHeader(name) == null ? List.of() : null;
671      var l = new ArrayList<String>();
672      while (e.hasMoreElements())
673         l.add(e.nextElement());
674      return l;
675   }
676
677   /**
678    * Whether a container's view {@code c} of the request is one the forwarded origin must not replace.
679    *
680    * <p>
681    * Used where the container's view is the transport (a handshake, or HTTP under {@code HOST_HEADER}): equal views
682    * agree, and an unequal one is replaced, except when its host is one the forwarded header carries to the left of the
683    * selected entry, or when such an entry did not parse (a container may normalize it into a host of its own), which
684    * means the container may have trusted a hop the client could have written.
685    */
686   private static boolean containerDisagrees(Origin c, ForwardedOrigin.Resolved f) {
687      return ! c.host().equals(f.origin().host()) && (f.leftUnparsed() || f.leftHosts().contains(c.host()));
688   }
689
690   /** The fixed text for a forwarded-host refusal. Visibility relaxed for testing. */
691   static String forwardedMessage(BoundaryReason reason) {
692      return switch (reason) {
693         case FORWARDED_HOST_MISSING -> "A trusted-forwarding boundary requires the forwarded host header; none was usable.";
694         case FORWARDED_PROTO_MISSING -> "A trusted-forwarding boundary requires the forwarded proto alongside the forwarded host.";
695         case FORWARDED_HOST_MALFORMED -> "The forwarded host header is malformed.";
696         case FORWARDED_PROTO_MALFORMED -> "The forwarded proto must be 'http' or 'https'.";
697         case FORWARDED_HOPS_INSUFFICIENT -> "The forwarded header holds fewer entries than the trusted hop count.";
698         case FORWARDED_HOPS_MISMATCH -> "The forwarded host and proto headers hold different numbers of entries.";
699         case FORWARDED_CONTAINER_MISMATCH -> "The container's view of the request disagrees with the forwarded origin.";
700         case FORWARDED_PEER_NOT_TRUSTED -> "The forwarded header was sent by a peer that is not a trusted proxy.";
701         default -> throw iaex("Not a forwarded-host reason: %s", reason);
702      };
703   }
704
705   /** The outcome of {@link #forwardedSelf}: the origin to judge against, or the refusal. */
706   private record Self(Origin origin, BoundaryResult refusal) {}
707
708   /** The own origin of an HTTP request when trusted forwarding is on. */
709   private Self forwardedSelf(HttpServletRequest req, String method, List<String> hosts) {
710      var host = hosts.size() == 1 ? BoundaryChecks.parseHost(hosts.get(0)) : null;
711      if (host == null)
712         return new Self(null, hostFailure(req, method, hosts));
713      var resolved = ForwardedOrigin.resolve(trustedForwarding, trustedHops, name -> forwardedLines(req, name));
714      if (resolved.reason() != null)
715         return new Self(null, refuse(req, method, resolved.reason(), 403, forwardedMessage(resolved.reason())));
716      var c = selfOrigin(req, host);
717      // Under CONTAINER the container is declared a forwarding authority, so its view must be exactly the forwarded one.
718      var disagrees = originSource == OriginSource.CONTAINER ? ! resolved.origin().equals(c) : containerDisagrees(c, resolved);
719      if (disagrees)
720         return new Self(null, refuse(req, method, BoundaryReason.FORWARDED_CONTAINER_MISMATCH, 403,
721            forwardedMessage(BoundaryReason.FORWARDED_CONTAINER_MISMATCH)));
722      return new Self(resolved.origin(), null);
723   }
724
725   /** Logs a refused handshake and builds its result.  {@code message} must be a fixed text, as for {@code refuse}. */
726   private static BoundaryResult refuseHandshake(BoundaryReason reason, int status, String message, HandshakeHosts hosts, List<String> origins,
727         Function<String,List<String>> forwardedHeaders, InetAddress peer) {
728      LOG.fine(() -> "CSRF boundary refused a WebSocket handshake: reason=" + reason
729         + ", peer=" + (peer == null ? "unknown" : sanitize(peer.getHostAddress())));
730      if (LOG.isLoggable(Level.FINEST))
731         LOG.finest("CSRF boundary refused a WebSocket handshake: reason=" + reason
732            + ", Origin=" + sanitize(String.join(", ", origins))
733            + ", Host=" + (hosts.synthesised() ? "(h2 :authority) " : "") + sanitize(String.join(", ", hosts.values()))
734            + (forwardedHeaders == null || ! reason.name().startsWith("FORWARDED_") ? "" : ", " + forwardedValues(forwardedHeaders)));
735      return new BoundaryResult(reason, status, message);
736   }
737
738   /** The forwarded header values of a request, as one sanitized log fragment; a name read as {@code null} is shown as such. */
739   private static String forwardedValues(Function<String,List<String>> lookup) {
740      var sb = new StringBuilder();
741      for (var name : new String[] { "X-Forwarded-Host", "X-Forwarded-Proto", "Forwarded" }) {
742         var lines = lookup.apply(name);
743         if (! sb.isEmpty())
744            sb.append(", ");
745         sb.append(name).append('=').append(lines == null ? "(unordered)" : sanitize(String.join(" | ", lines)));
746      }
747      return sb.toString();
748   }
749
750   /** The token and JSON checks for a request that came from a page, or that the policy holds to a page's rules. */
751   private BoundaryResult checkBrowser(HttpServletRequest req, String method, boolean originMatched) {
752      if (requireJson && ! isSingleJson(req))
753         return refuseNotJson(req, method);
754
755      var presented = BoundaryChecks.headerValues(req, csrfHeader);
756      if (presented.isEmpty() || (presented.size() == 1 && presented.get(0).isBlank())) {
757         if (originMatched && MISSING_FROM_OWN_ORIGIN.get() < MISSING_TOKEN_WARN_AT
758               && MISSING_FROM_OWN_ORIGIN.incrementAndGet() == MISSING_TOKEN_WARN_AT)
759            LOG.log(Level.WARNING, "CSRF boundary: {0} requests from this server''s own origin arrived without the ''{1}'' header.  Does the page embed the token, or is this an HTML form POST?",
760               new Object[] { String.valueOf(MISSING_TOKEN_WARN_AT), csrfHeader });
761         return refuse(req, method, BoundaryReason.CSRF_TOKEN_MISSING, 403,
762            "A state-changing request must carry the CSRF token in the '" + csrfHeader + "' header.");
763      }
764      // The same answer whether or not a session exists: with none, the comparison is against a value nothing matches.
765      if (presented.size() != 1 || ! tokens.verify(presented.get(0), tokens.expected(req, false)))
766         return refuse(req, method, BoundaryReason.CSRF_TOKEN_MISMATCH, 403,
767            "The CSRF token in the '" + csrfHeader + "' header is not valid for this request.");
768
769      return BoundaryResult.ALLOWED;
770   }
771
772   /**
773    * The request's own origin, or <jk>null</jk> if it cannot be derived.
774    *
775    * @param host The parsed {@code Host} header, or <jk>null</jk> if it is malformed.  Required in both modes, because
776    *    {@code getServerName()} falls back to the server's own name when the request has no {@code Host}.  On HTTP/2, which
777    *    has none, it is the server name and port the container derived from {@code :authority}.
778    */
779   private Origin selfOrigin(HttpServletRequest req, Authority host) {
780      if (host == null)
781         return null;
782      var scheme = req.getScheme() == null ? null : req.getScheme().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
783      if (originSource == OriginSource.CONTAINER) {
784         // Tomcat reports an IPv6 server name without the brackets a Host header would carry.
785         var serverName = req.getServerName();
786         if (serverName != null && serverName.indexOf(':') >= 0 && ! serverName.startsWith("["))
787            serverName = "[" + serverName + "]";
788         var name = BoundaryChecks.parseHost(serverName);
789         if (name == null || name.port() >= 0)
790            return null;
791         var port = req.getServerPort();
792         return new Origin(scheme, name.host(), port > 0 ? port : BoundaryChecks.defaultPort(scheme));
793      }
794      return new Origin(scheme, host.host(), host.port() >= 0 ? host.port() : BoundaryChecks.defaultPort(scheme));
795   }
796
797   /** Non-simple in the CORS sense: a browser would have preflighted it cross-site. */
798   private static boolean isNonSimple(HttpServletRequest req) {
799      var m = req.getMethod() == null ? null : req.getMethod().toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
800      if (m != null && ! SIMPLE_METHODS.contains(m))
801         return true;
802      // Counted, never read through getContentType(): two headers can be reported as one non-form value.
803      var types = BoundaryChecks.headerValues(req, "Content-Type");
804      return types.size() == 1 && ! types.get(0).isBlank() && types.get(0).indexOf(',') < 0
805         && ! BoundaryChecks.isSafelistedType(types.get(0));
806   }
807
808   private static boolean isSingleJson(HttpServletRequest req) {
809      var types = BoundaryChecks.headerValues(req, "Content-Type");
810      return types.size() == 1 && BoundaryChecks.isJson(types.get(0));
811   }
812
813   private static boolean isSameOriginFetch(List<String> values) {
814      return values.size() == 1 && BoundaryChecks.isSameOriginFetch(values.get(0));
815   }
816
817   private static BoundaryResult hostFailure(HttpServletRequest req, String method, List<String> hosts) {
818      if (hosts.isEmpty())
819         return refuse(req, method, BoundaryReason.HOST_MISSING, 400, "A request must carry a 'Host' header (or, on HTTP/2, ':authority').");
820      return refuse(req, method, BoundaryReason.HOST_MALFORMED, 400,
821         "Request 'Host' must be a single header holding a host name, IPv4 address or bracketed IPv6 address, "
822         + "with an optional port.");
823   }
824
825   private static BoundaryResult refuseFetchSite(HttpServletRequest req, String method) {
826      return refuse(req, method, BoundaryReason.FETCH_SITE_NOT_SAME_ORIGIN, 403,
827         "Request 'Sec-Fetch-Site' must be a single 'same-origin' value when present on a state-changing request.");
828   }
829
830   private static BoundaryResult refuseNotJson(HttpServletRequest req, String method) {
831      return refuse(req, method, BoundaryReason.CONTENT_TYPE_NOT_JSON, 415,
832         "A state-changing request must carry a single 'Content-Type' of 'application/json'.");
833   }
834
835   /**
836    * Logs the refusal and builds its result.
837    *
838    * <p>
839    * {@code message} must be a fixed text naming only headers and the kind of value expected.
840    */
841   private static BoundaryResult refuse(HttpServletRequest req, String method, BoundaryReason reason, int status, String message) {
842      if (LOG.isLoggable(Level.FINE))
843         LOG.fine("CSRF boundary refused a request: reason=" + reason
844            + ", method=" + sanitize(method)
845            + ", requestMethod=" + sanitize(req.getMethod())
846            + ", uri=" + sanitize(pathOnly(req.getRequestURI()))
847            + ", remoteAddr=" + sanitize(req.getRemoteAddr()));
848      if (LOG.isLoggable(Level.FINEST))
849         LOG.finest("CSRF boundary refused a request: reason=" + reason
850            + ", Origin=" + sanitize(String.join(", ", BoundaryChecks.headerValues(req, "Origin")))
851            + ", Host=" + (BoundaryChecks.isSynthesisedHost(req) ? "(h2 :authority) " : "")
852            + sanitize(String.join(", ", BoundaryChecks.hostValues(req)))
853            + (reason.name().startsWith("FORWARDED_") ? ", " + forwardedValues(name -> forwardedLines(req, name)) : ""));
854      return new BoundaryResult(reason, status, message);
855   }
856
857   /** One warning per process for an Origin that differs from the own origin only in the way a misconfiguration would. */
858   private static void warnNearMiss(Origin presented, Origin self) {
859      if (! presented.host().equals(self.host()))
860         return;
861      if (! presented.scheme().equals(self.scheme())) {
862         if (SCHEME_WARNED.compareAndSet(false, true))
863            LOG.warning("CSRF boundary: a request's 'Origin' differs from this server's own origin only in its scheme.  "
864               + "TLS terminated upstream?  See originSource(CONTAINER) and filter ordering.");
865      } else if (presented.port() != self.port() && PORT_WARNED.compareAndSet(false, true)) {
866         LOG.warning("CSRF boundary: a request's 'Origin' differs from this server's own origin only in its port.  "
867            + "Is a proxy or port mapping rewriting 'Host'?");
868      }
869   }
870
871   /** The URI with any query and any {@code ;} path parameters (where a container may put a session id) cut off. */
872   private static String pathOnly(String uri) {
873      if (uri == null)
874         return null;
875      var end = uri.length();
876      for (var c : new char[] { '?', ';', '#' }) {
877         var i = uri.indexOf(c);
878         if (i >= 0 && i < end)
879            end = i;
880      }
881      return uri.substring(0, end);
882   }
883
884   /** A value safe for one log line: control characters removed, at most {@value #MAX_LOGGED} characters. */
885   private static String sanitize(String value) {
886      if (value == null)
887         return "null";
888      var sb = new StringBuilder(Math.min(value.length(), MAX_LOGGED));
889      for (var i = 0; i < value.length() && sb.length() < MAX_LOGGED; i++) {
890         var c = value.charAt(i);
891         if (c >= 0x20 && c != 0x7f)
892            sb.append(c);
893      }
894      return sb.toString();
895   }

897   /**
898    * Clears the once-per-process warning state, so each warning can be observed again.
899    */
900   static void resetWarnings() {
901      SCHEME_WARNED.set(false);
902      PORT_WARNED.set(false);
903      MISSING_FROM_OWN_ORIGIN.set(0);

906   /**
907    * A freshly masked token for the page being served to this request.
908    *
909    * <p>
910    * Never creates a session: with a session-scoped strategy and no session, the value returned verifies against
911    * nothing.  Creating the session, when that is wanted, is {@link RequestBoundaryFilter}'s job.
912    *
913    * @param req The request whose response will embed the token.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
914    * @return 128 lower-case hex characters, different on every call.
915    */
916   @Override /* RequestBoundary */
917   public String tokenFor(HttpServletRequest req) {
918      reqnn("req", req);
919      return tokens.mask(tokens.expected(req, false));
920   }

1003   /**
1004    * Builder for {@link CsrfBoundary}.
1005    */
1006   public static class Builder {
1007
1008      CsrfTokens tokens;
1009      NonBrowser nonBrowser = NonBrowser.ADMIT_NON_SIMPLE;
1010      OriginSource originSource = OriginSource.HOST_HEADER;
1011      boolean requireJson;
1012      Set<String> allowedHosts = Set.of();
1013      String csrfHeader = LoopbackBoundary.DEFAULT_CSRF_HEADER;
1014      boolean createSessions = true;
1015      ForwardedSource trustedForwarding = ForwardedSource.NONE;
1016      int trustedHops = 1;
1017      PeerRanges trustedProxies;
1018
1019      /**
1020       * Constructor.
1021       */
1022      protected Builder() {}
1023
1024      /**
1025       * The token strategy.
1026       *
1027       * @param value The strategy.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.  Defaults to a new {@link CsrfTokens#perSession()}.
1028       * @return This object.
1029       */
1030      public Builder tokens(CsrfTokens value) {
1031         tokens = reqnn("value", value);
1032         return this;
1033      }
1034
1035      /**
1036       * The policy for unsafe requests with neither {@code Origin} nor {@code Sec-Fetch-Site}.
1037       *
1038       * @param value The policy.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.  Defaults to {@link NonBrowser#ADMIT_NON_SIMPLE}.
1039       * @return This object.
1040       */
1041      public Builder nonBrowser(NonBrowser value) {
1042         nonBrowser = reqnn("value", value);
1043         return this;
1044      }
1045
1046      /**
1047       * Where the request's own origin comes from.
1048       *
1049       * @param value The source.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.  Defaults to {@link OriginSource#HOST_HEADER}.
1050       * @return This object.
1051       */
1052      public Builder originSource(OriginSource value) {
1053         originSource = reqnn("value", value);
1054         return this;
1055      }
1056
1057      /**
1058       * Whether every admitted unsafe request must carry a single {@code application/json} content type.
1059       *
1060       * <p>
1061       * Applies to browser and admitted non-browser requests alike.  Parameters are allowed; {@code +json} types are
1062       * not.
1063       *
1064       * @param value The setting.  Defaults to <jk>false</jk>.
1065       * @return This object.
1066       */
1067      public Builder requireJson(boolean value) {
1068         requireJson = value;
1069         return this;
1070      }
1071
1072      /**
1073       * The host names this server answers to.  When set, every request, safe ones included, whose own host is not
1074       * one of them is refused with {@code 421 HOST_NOT_ALLOWED}.
1075       *
1076       * <p>
1077       * Matching is case-insensitive and ignores the port.  A trailing-dot variant is a different name.  Replaces any
1078       * earlier list.  This is the DNS-rebinding control for applications served over plain HTTP.
1079       *
1080       * @param values Host names with no port, e.g. {@code "app.example.com"} or {@code "[::1]"}.  Must not be
1081       *    <jk>null</jk>, and no entry may be <jk>null</jk> or blank.
1082       * @return This object.
1083       * @throws IllegalArgumentException If {@code values} or an entry is <jk>null</jk>, blank, or not a bare host.
1084       */
1085      public Builder allowedHosts(String...values) {
1086         reqnn("values", values);
1087         var s = new LinkedHashSet<String>();
1088         for (var v : values) {
1089            reqnn("values", v);
1090            if (v.isBlank())
1091               throw iaex("Argument 'values' must not contain a blank entry.");
1092            var a = BoundaryChecks.parseHost(v.trim());
1093            if (a == null || a.port() >= 0)
1094               throw iaex("Argument 'values' must hold bare host names with no port.");
1095            s.add(a.host());
1096         }
1097         allowedHosts = s;
1098         return this;
1099      }
1100
1101      /**
1102       * The header an unsafe request must carry the CSRF token in.
1103       *
1104       * @param value The header name.  Must not be <jk>null</jk> or blank.  Defaults to
1105       *    {@link LoopbackBoundary#DEFAULT_CSRF_HEADER}.
1106       * @return This object.
1107       */
1108      public Builder csrfHeader(String value) {
1109         reqnn("value", value);
1110         if (value.isBlank())
1111            throw iaex("Argument 'value' must not be blank.");
1112         csrfHeader = value.trim();
1113         return this;
1114      }
1115
1116      /**
1117       * Whether {@link RequestBoundaryFilter} may create a session so that a page it serves can carry a
1118       * session-scoped token.  Has no effect with a per-process token strategy.
1119       *
1120       * @param value The setting.  Defaults to <jk>true</jk>.
1121       * @return This object.
1122       */
1123      public Builder createSessions(boolean value) {
1124         createSessions = value;
1125         return this;
1126      }
1127
1128      /**
1129       * Trusts the forwarded origin one proxy header family carries, for HTTP requests and WebSocket handshakes alike.
1130       *
1131       * <p>
1132       * With a source other than {@link ForwardedSource#NONE}, the request's own origin is the forwarded host
1133       * <b>and</b> proto of that one family, and nothing else: there is no fallback to {@code Host} or
1134       * {@code getScheme()}, and {@code X-Forwarded-Port} is never read.  A request missing either value, or with a
1135       * malformed one, is refused with a {@code FORWARDED_*} reason.  See {@link #trustedHops(int)} for how an entry
1136       * is selected.
1137       *
1138       * <p>
1139       * <b>Turn this on only if every request reaches the server through a proxy that removes or appends after any
1140       * client-supplied copy of the header.</b>  A server clients can reach directly lets them choose the origin.
1141       * See also {@link #trustedProxies(String...)} to believe only a listed peer address.
1142       *
1143       * @param value The source.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.  Defaults to {@link ForwardedSource#NONE}.
1144       * @return This object.
1145       */
1146      public Builder trustedForwarding(ForwardedSource value) {
1147         trustedForwarding = reqnn("value", value);
1148         return this;
1149      }
1150
1151      /**
1152       * The number of proxies that <i>append</i> to the forwarded header.
1153       *
1154       * <p>
1155       * The entries of the header are counted in wire order across all its lines and commas, and the {@code n}th from
1156       * the right is used; entries to its left are ignored.  A chain of proxies that overwrite the header stays at 1.
1157       * <b>Never set this above the number of proxies that append:</b> an overstated value selects an entry the client
1158       * wrote, and that fails open.  An understated value selects an inner hop and only causes refusals.
1159       *
1160       * @param value The hop count, 1 to 16.  Defaults to 1.
1161       * @return This object.
1162       * @throws IllegalArgumentException If {@code value} is outside 1 to 16.
1163       */
1164      public Builder trustedHops(int value) {
1165         if (value < 1 || value > 16)
1166            throw iaex("Argument 'value' must be between 1 and 16.");
1167         trustedHops = value;
1168         return this;
1169      }
1170
1171      /**
1172       * Believes the forwarded headers only from peers in these address ranges.
1173       *
1174       * <p>
1175       * Without this, {@link #trustedForwarding(ForwardedSource)} believes the forwarded headers from whoever sends
1176       * them.  With it, the peer address the container reports (HTTP: {@link HttpServletRequest#getRemoteAddr()}) must
1177       * be in a range.  A request from another peer that carries a forwarded host in the selected family is refused
1178       * ({@code FORWARDED_PEER_NOT_TRUSTED}); one that does not is judged on the container's own view, as if forwarding
1179       * were off.  A peer that cannot be parsed, or that the container did not report, is not trusted.
1180       *
1181       * <p>
1182       * Each entry is an IPv4 or IPv6 literal with an optional {@code /prefix}.  Host bits are masked
1183       * ({@code 10.0.0.1/8} is {@code 10.0.0.0/8}); {@code /0} trusts every peer of its family.  Names are never
1184       * resolved, and a bracketed form, a zone id or an IPv4-mapped IPv6 form is refused (write the IPv4 form).  An IPv4-mapped IPv6 peer
1185       * is matched as the IPv4 address it carries.
1186       *
1187       * <p>
1188       * Use this only where the container reports the TCP peer: it is meaningless, or unsafe, where the container
1189       * rewrites the peer from a header (Jetty's {@code ForwardedRequestCustomizer}, Tomcat's {@code RemoteIpValve},
1190       * the PROXY protocol).  On WebSocket handshakes the peer comes from {@link #checkHandshake(String, HandshakeHosts, Map, java.net.InetAddress)};
1191       * a container that supplies none (Tomcat) refuses every handshake that carries a forwarded host.
1192       *
1193       * @param cidrs The ranges.  At least one; none may be <jk>null</jk> or invalid.  Replaces any earlier list.
1194       * @return This object.
1195       * @throws IllegalArgumentException If there are no ranges or one is invalid.
1196       */
1197      public Builder trustedProxies(String...cidrs) {
1198         trustedProxies = new PeerRanges(cidrs);
1199         return this;
1200      }
1201
1202      /**
1203       * Builds the boundary.
1204       *
1205       * @return A new {@link CsrfBoundary}.
1206       * @throws IllegalArgumentException If {@link #trustedHops(int)} is not 1 while no forwarded source is trusted,
1207       *    or if {@link #trustedProxies(String...)} is set without a forwarded source or with
1208       *    {@link OriginSource#CONTAINER}.
1209       */
1210      public CsrfBoundary build() {
1211         if (trustedHops != 1 && trustedForwarding == ForwardedSource.NONE)
1212            throw iaex("trustedHops requires trustedForwarding.");
1213         if (trustedProxies != null && trustedForwarding == ForwardedSource.NONE)
1214            throw iaex("trustedProxies requires trustedForwarding.");
1215         if (trustedProxies != null && originSource == OriginSource.CONTAINER)
1216            throw iaex("trustedProxies cannot be combined with originSource(CONTAINER): the container is then the forwarding authority.");
1217         return new CsrfBoundary(this);
1218      }
1219   }
1220}
